title: Bias in Gender Bias Benchmarks: How Spurious Features Distort Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: The paper measures gender bias in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using two main methods: 1) Visual Question Answering (VQA) evaluation for generative VLMs using the YGap metric, which compares the probability of models assigning specific personality traits, skills, and occupations to male versus female images; 2) Text-to-image retrieval evaluation for CLIP variants using the MaxSkew metric, which measures deviations in the gender proportions of retrieved images for gender-neutral prompts. The core methodology of the paper involves applying controlled feature perturbations (modifying color, lighting, objects, and backgrounds) to evaluate how sensitive and distorted these gender bias metrics are to spurious non-gender features.
